variant_decisions.evidence: ASV renders the name 'Hiram', which transliterates the ketiv חירם (with yod, i-vowel); the qere חוּרָם (with waw, u-vowel) would yield 'Huram'. The English spelling distinguishes the readings and follows the ketiv.

mimmûl rendered by the one compound 'over against' (rule 30). Both morphemes are tagged R, so this is rule 23's compound preposition written from two prepositions: the syntactic head is the one standing first, exactly as mēʿal heads on min whatever English it takes. Competing head: mûl (s026) as the morpheme carrying the 'opposite' sense. Target head on against, the word carrying the relation (rule 24).

'mulberry trees' for one noun: dropping trees leaves mulberry still naming the species, dropping mulberry leaves any tree, and the ASV never writes trees alone for bākāʾ, so the head goes on the specifier exactly as timōrāh → palm trees heads on palm (rule 31). Competing head trees as the class word; margin 'balsam-trees' read and set aside (rule 38).
